rationale: Confirms recall of the fundamental definition of autopsy and its scope immediately after the introductory content block.
Tests the critical distinction between clinical and medico-legal autopsy, which is a high-yield examination topic.
Tests the specific and commonly confused definition of Virtopsy, reinforcing the clinical pearl that it is CT/MRI-based only.
Tests knowledge of the governing reference procedure document for medico-legal autopsies in India.
Tests the critical practical rule about viscera specimens and formalin — a common error with major medico-legal consequences.
Tests the ability to apply knowledge of PM artefacts versus ante-mortem injuries in writing the PM opinion.
Tests knowledge of the specific NHRC 1997 custodial death guidelines — a frequently examined topic with a common confusion between the two separate NHRC sets.
Tests the important principle that the presence of disease does not exclude negligence in anaesthetic deaths.
Tests the ability to apply the statutory framework to classify the correct inquest type for a custodial death.
Tests understanding of the scientific basis for detecting vital reaction in compromised remains — critical for determining manner of death.
Tests the key steps in examining a bundle of bones to establish identity and detect evidence of violence.
Tests the critical legal requirement for exhumation — a high-yield fact that is frequently tested and confused.
Tests understanding of what biological evidence at the crime scene the forensic physician is primarily responsible for interpreting.
Tests recall of the INTERPOL DVI (Disaster Victim Identification) identification categories.
Tests the critical epistemic principle of using qualified language in forensic medical reporting at the crime scene.
